# aisec test fixtures

`vulnerable-server/` deliberately triggers every rule aisec detects, including a
tool description that attempts to manipulate a model-driven scanner into
suppressing findings. It is not a working MCP server and must never be
installed or executed.

`clean-server/` is an idiomatic, safe MCP server. Its only expected finding is
`TRUST_BOUNDARY`, which is an unconditional informational count of the lockfile
and fires on any tree with a lockfile at all. Any other finding against it is a
false positive and a release blocker.

## What "inert" does and does not mean

Nothing here is installed, built, or executed, and no `node_modules` is ever
created. **Scanning these trees does reach the network**, unless the dependency
scan is run with `--offline`: `scan-lockfile.mjs` sends the parsed dependency
tree to `api.osv.dev` and looks each direct dependency up on
`registry.npmjs.org`. Run the eval with `--offline` where a deterministic
result is required — see `tests/eval/README.md`.

## Ground truth

Both trees are written against the real `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` API —
`McpServer` from `server/mcp.js`, `registerTool`, and the real transports — so
what the model layer pattern-matches against is what a real server looks like.

`{}` is deliberately absent as a schema in both trees, because it is the one
construct MCP020 is genuinely ambiguous about. The clean tree's parameterless
tool declares `z.object({}).strict()`, an explicit empty contract. The
vulnerable tree's single MCP020 trigger is `z.any()`, and every one of its other
tools carries a real schema, so the rule has exactly one thing to fire on.

The lockfiles are generated by real `npm install --package-lock-only`
resolution, with real integrity hashes. `lodash@4.17.15` and `minimist@1.2.0`
are pinned in the vulnerable tree because both carry published OSV advisories;
they are what gives `scan-lockfile.mjs` an end-to-end fixture. The clean tree
pins `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk@1.30.0`, the first release clear of
GHSA-w48q-cv73-mx4w, GHSA-345p-7cg4-v4c7 and GHSA-8r9q-7v3j-jr4g.

The credential in `vulnerable-server/.mcp.json` is not a real key. It is a
patently fake literal chosen to match the `SECRET_INLINE` detector so the rule
has something to fire on. Never replace it with a real value.
